characters.name: Waddles
characters.description: Mabel's beloved pet pig. She wins him at the Mystery Shack's fair after guessing his weight (which was blatantly given away by his name, Ol' 15-Poundie). Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: In "Summerween" at least, where Mabel dresses him up like a businessman. This later becomes the subject of aCredits Gaginvolvinglolpigs. Also used in one of the Life According To Mabel shorts, where she dresses him in exercise clothes as part of her Jog Hog segment. Big Eater: As is typical of cartoon pigs, he's capable of eating quite a lot. Black Bead Eyes: His most common trait, along with a few other animals in Gravity Falls. When Soos ends up in his body in "Carpet Diem," his eyes become large with sclera around the pupils. The same thing happens with Dipper and later, Mabel. Cuteness Overload: He has this effect on Mabel, causing her toSqueefrequently about him.

characters.name: Gompers
characters.description: A goat usually found on the Mystery Shack property. All There in the Manual: The reason he's at the Shack at all, as a cut scene from "Blendin's Game" would've revealed, is that a tourist to the Mystery Shack attempted to use a baby Gompers as payment, and the goat just stayed there ever since. Ambiguously Evil: Bill Cipher claims in his Reddit AMA that Gompers is something more ancient and eldritch than even him. That said, we can never really trust what Bill says, and the show doesn't depict him doing anything particularly malicious, at least directly. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever:Bill's weirdness wave in "Weirdmageddon Part 1"turns him into a giant version of himself who tramples through the area around the Mystery Shack,forcing Stan to flee for his life. Chekhov's Gunman:Plays a very minor but substantial role in the episode "Boyz Crazy," in which he eats Ergman Bratsman's license plate, gets the manager arrested.In"Weirdmageddon Part 1",after being turned giant,he eats part of the prison wall, freeing Gideon and his fellow inmates.

characters.name: "Old Man"McGucket
characters.description: Fiddleford HadronMcGucket, better known as Old ManMcGucketis (self-) described as the town's "local kook." The description is...apt, but limited. He represents the spectacles on the Zodiac for being scholarly. All for Nothing:He continually erases his mind to forget witnessing Bill Cipher's true plans. He ends up becoming an insane hermit, and as the tape of his continued memory erasure shows, the only remaining memory of his past life is a vague one of Bill Cipher."EHEHEHE! YROO XRKSVI GIRZMTOV!" (continues laughing as he makes a triangle shape with his fingers and puts it on his eye) Ambiguously Bi: OrAmbiguously Gay, and entirely relegated toThe Book of Bill.His relationship with his wife is already on the rocks by the time Ford invites him out to work in Gravity Falls, and he seems to have an ambiguous two-timing thing going on with Ford, at least emotionally. He gets in a fight with his wife that Christmas after hand-making not one buttwothoughtful gifts for Ford, and neglecting to get her anything. In the show itself, he mentions that his wife left him. He made a giant robot in revenge. Ambiguously Evil: He's usually harmless and even friendly towards Dipper and Mabel, but he has admitted that he's gone on homicidal rampages before without being caught. Ancient Conspiracy:Founded the Society of the Blind Eyeas a way to help people forget their terrible memories, andinvented the Society's Memory Gun.

characters.name: Sheriff Blubs and Deputy Durland
characters.description: The law of Gravity Falls. True to the tradition of fictional small town cops, they are mostlyuseless. Action Survivor:Sheriff Blubs manages to avoid getting captured by Bill, surviving three days into Weirdmageddon and reaching the Mystery Shack alongside the other survivors. He later took part in the attack on the Fearamid to rescue Ford and the people of Gravity Falls. Ambiguously Gay: Some of the comments Blubs makes directed at Durland in "Irrational Treasure" may lend themselves to one side of ambiguous. Then there's the vacation they go on at the end of the episode... together.The finale gleefully discards any and all ambiguity. Big Ol' Unibrow: Durland's got a unibrow. Characterisation Marches On: In their early episodes, Blubs and Durland are depicted antagonistically, mocking Dipper and brushing off his concerns in 'Headhunters' and later being prepared to send Dipper and Mabel off to Washington after the twins uncover the truth about Trembley. In later episodes, they're far nicer and less antagonistic, and they show absolutelynointerest in actually policing.

characters.name: Manly Dan
characters.description: A lumberjack and fisherman. Also Wendy's father. Always a Bigger Fish:He flees from the Manotaurs, who are even more manly than he is.The opening of "Weirdmageddon Part 1" shows him visibly frightened by the arrival ofBill Cipher, although he does join the town inthreatening himin their initial push back. He flees from the Manotaurs, who are even more manly than he is. The opening of "Weirdmageddon Part 1" shows him visibly frightened by the arrival ofBill Cipher, although he does join the town inthreatening himin their initial push back. Badass Normal: He's a blue-collar worker with immense physical power. When handling Stan's bear, it breaks free, and Dan responds by putting it in a headlock. Mabel thinks he's giving it a hug.

characters.name: Tyler Cutebiker
characters.description: A guy seen hanging around Manly Dan a lot, though generally he seems to show up whenever a fight breaks out. Alternate Catchphrase Inflection: His "Get 'im! Get 'im!" is normally enthusiastic and excited, but when he realizes that Gideon is a con-artist who's been exploiting the town and playing them for fools, his order to "get 'im" is morose and heartbroken to the point of wiping away tears. Ambiguously Gay: He often hangs around Manly Dan and seems overly fond of him, and could be seen screaming along with a bunch of girls at a Sev'ral Timez concert. He's also one of the Love God's groupies. Badass Biker:Hilariouslysubverted. Even when hanging out in a biker bar, he keeps an absurdly cheerful demeanor. Boring, but Practical: In "The Stanchurian Candidate,"he wins the election for mayor not with any crazy campaigns or displays of charisma, but because he filed his paperwork correctly.

characters.name: Toby Determined
characters.description: The journalist, editor, and manager for a newspaper called theGravity Falls Gossiper. Abhorrent Admirer: Shandra considers him this. Action Survivor: Manages to survive 3 days in Weirdmageddon and manages to reach the Shack by day 5 by himself. Adrenaline Makeover: He tries to invoke this in "Weirdmageddon" by giving himself a blue mohawk and dressing like a teenage punk, but he's just as incompetent as always. At least it seems to do something for his self-confidence, as he chooses to keep his new look and the self-styled nickname of "Bodacious T" after everything else returns to normal. Ancient Conspiracy: A member ofthe Society of the Blind Eye.

characters.name: "Lazy" Susan Wentworth
characters.description: Waitress at the localGreasy Spoon, "Greasy's Diner". Not exactly the brightest crayon in the box, even for Gravity Falls. Abhorrent Admirer: Made Grunkle Stan flee their first date, then left 36 voice messages on his phone. Cerebus Retcon:Having her mind wipedis probably what made her crazy. Similarly, her lazy eye is revealed to have been caused byone of Stanford's machines zapping her eye during Grunkle Stan's first "tour" of his house. Cloudcuckoolander: Pours coffee in her omelets."The secret to my Coffee Omelet is coffee!" Crazy Cat Lady: Makes her cats meow over the phone when leaving messages.

characters.name: Shandra Jimenez
characters.description: The female news reporter of Gravity Falls, and unwilling target of Toby Determined's secret affection. Badass Normal: It's downplayed, but whenBill takes over the town and causes the Weirdmageddon, Shandra keeps right on going, surviving a few days into the end of the world, still reporting the news, and very bravely breaks into Bill's lair to show the citizens of Gravity Falls what's going on. And when she gets turned to stone, she takes it with dignity.Hard not to respect her after that. Catchphrase:"Shandra Jimenez, arealreporter". (glances in Toby's direction)"I'm Shandra Jimenez, and I'm (insert whatever she's doing or happening to her at the moment.)" Heard only in parts 1 and 3 of the finale. "Shandra Jimenez, arealreporter". (glances in Toby's direction) "I'm Shandra Jimenez, and I'm (insert whatever she's doing or happening to her at the moment.)" Heard only in parts 1 and 3 of the finale.

characters.name: Abuelita Ramirez
characters.description: Soos' elderly grandmother, a very calm and soft-spoken woman who takes things in great stride, which is impressive considering she lives in Gravity Falls. Ambiguously Christian: MentionsHeaven, impliesHell, and has a bunch of porcelain angels. Awful Wedded Life: Implied to be the case with Soos' grandfather. Abuelita is apparently quite certain that she won't be reuniting with him in Heaven. Doting Grandparent: Downplayed, but in "Mabel's Guide to Dating", Soos says this about her after he scores a 12 at Mabel's test:Soos:My grandma was right all along! I am the world's most perfect man. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": "Abuelita" is just the Spanish diminutive of "grandmother". Her given name was revealed in the Journals.

characters.name: Melody
characters.description: A girl from Portland who is visiting Gravity Falls for a while, and working at the "Meat Cute" stall at the mall. She ends up dating Soos after she sees him riding a toy train just outside her work. Unbeknownst to them, however, is that it resulted in inciting the wrath of Giffany. Action Girl: There's no indication she's ever brushed with the supernatural, and yet when faced with murderous animatronics, shepicks up a chair and smashes one over the head with itbefore being overwhelmed. Ambiguously Brown: Her skin is light brown, but it's unclear if she's just tanned or if she's of a non-white ethnicity. Big Beautiful Woman: She's definitely a plus-size girl, but this has no effect on her natural beauty, and she wears clothes that flatter her build. Plus, obviously, Soos thinks she looks nice enough to date. Birds of a Feather: With Soos. She’s also childish for her age, enjoys a good meal, and is very nice, friendly, and loyal. She first steps up to talk to him after seeing him riding a toy train, finding it awesome.

characters.name: Mayor Eustace "Huckabone" Befufftlefumpter
characters.description: The reclusive mayor of Gravity Falls; Eustace Hucklebone Befufftlefumpter is 102 years old, and, consequentially, is "not long for this earth". Been There, Shaped History: Allegedly started World War I. Big Ol' Eyebrows: Has thick eyebrows. Character Death:In "The Stanchurian Candidate", but he's reanimated as a zombie by the effects of the apocalyptic Weirdmageddon. Creator Cameo: The Mayor is yet another character voiced by the creator of the series.

characters.name: Tad Strange
characters.description: The most normal guy in Gravity Falls. Always with You: According to Alex Hirsch, " Although Tad won't be back for a while, rest assured that whenever you buy milk, paint something white, or stare at a nondescript rock, Tad is there in spirit. And ladies, he's single!” Attempted Homewrecker:On thisisnotawebsitedotcom.com, Soos claims that Tad Strange has a crush on Woodpecker Guy, who is already married. To a woodpecker. Bit Character:According to Alex Hirsch, he's in the show mostly because of a joke about hisIronic Name. Hissurprising popularity, and voice actor's fanbase on the internet netted him another appearance in Weirdmageddon. The Cameo: His voice actor is the voice of the main character ofWelcome to Night Vale.

characters.name: Farmer Sprott
characters.description: A farmer and the original owner of Waddles. Absurd Phobia: Is deeply afraid of witches. Ancient Conspiracy: A member ofthe Society of the Blind Eye. Apocalypse Cult: He starts worshipping Bill during the events of Weirdmageddon, declaring that any object with more than three sides is sinful in Bill's eyes and encouraging bystanders to make everything into triangles to try and appease him. He is, of course, just as wrong about what Bill wants as Preston Northwest. Comedic Sociopath: He’s usually a bit too eager to be rallied into an act of violence, such as gathering a mob to go after Mabel, or sadistically waxing about how he’s going to eat his mutated cow.

characters.name: Free Pizza Guy
characters.description: A resident of Gravity Falls who always struggles to get a free meal. Big Eater: His main focus scenes revolve around his desire to get something to eat, and he evidently eats a lot considering he's so rotund that he's even bigger than Soos, who is already considerably heavyset. Gideon's security footage of him, unsurprisingly, is of him eating his beloved pizza. Butt-Monkey: Tries and often fails to get a meal in peace. Character Tic: Whenever he’s disappointed by something, he lets out a sad sigh. Establishing Character Moment: His introduction in "Headhunters" shows him having donned a shirt that said "Free Pizza" in celebration of the free pizza being promised by Stan, only for him to sigh sadly and walk home crushed when it turns out to have been a lie.

characters.name: Mr. Poolcheck
characters.description: The head lifeguard of the Gravity Falls Public Pool. He takes his jobveryseriously. Ambiguously Human: He is inhumanly strong, able to tear through metal fences and do push ups with his fingers, he is able to destroy a metal whistle with his teeth, he drinks chlorinated pool water, his hand is artificial...but he's never confirmed as anything other than a very athletic and very weird human. An Arm and a Leg: He lost his right hand to a pool filter. Badass Normal: He's one of the last few unpetrified townspeople outside the Mystery Shack in "Weirdmageddon Part 3", meaning that he's managed to survive marauding eye-bats, hungry monsters, and wandering madness bubbles for several days. Barrier-Busting Blow: He plows clean through a chain-link fence in pursuit of Soos.

characters.name: Candy and Grenda
characters.description: A pair of girls who befriend Mabel. Action Girl: Grenda proves herself as this in "Summerween" and "Dungeons, Dungeons and More Dungeons". Candy has shades of this as well. Candy shows more than this in "Roadside Attraction". Alliterative Name: Both —CandyChiu andGrendaGrendinator. Badass Adorable: Downplayed; they don't often play a major part in the conflicts, but the one time they did, they proved to do quite well. Beauty, Brains, and Brawn: Candy's the Brains and Grenda's the Brawn to Mabel's Beauty.

characters.name: Wendy and Robbie's Friends
characters.description: Wendy and Robbie's friends and local youth. Ambiguously Brown: Nate and Tambry both have darker skin than their friends, but their ethnicities haven't been confirmed. It is implied that Nate is African-American and Tambry isprobablyeither Hispanic, South Asian, or both mixed. Creator Cameo: Lee and Thompson are voiced by Michael Rianda, a former writer and creative director for the show, while Alex Hirsch voiced Natein Season 2. Flat Character: While Robbie and Wendy have had prominent roles, the rest of the teens have only had a major part in"The Inconveniencing", and otherwise have little characterization outside of common teen stereotypes. Season two gave them more development, mainly in "The Love God". Recurring Extra: Often seen in the background or given minor roles.

characters.name: Gorney
characters.description: A little kid that shows up on Summerweenonly to get eaten by the Summerween Trickster.He turns out to be fine. Back for the Finale: Is seen lying in a cot in the Mystery Shack refugee camp in theGrand Finale. The Cameo: Briefly shows up at the party in "Scary-oke". Eaten Alive: As the end of the episode shows, he was alive the entire time after being devoured by the Trickster. Elmuh Fudd Syndwome: Most noticable when he says "Twik-owr-tweet!", and later when he cheerfully exclaims"I've been twaumatized!"after being freed from the Summerween Trickster.

characters.name: Gabe Bensen
characters.description: A local puppeteer who takes his craft very seriously. All of the Other Reindeer: It’s implied he has a history of being mocked for his puppet fetish, saying that people used to call him "puppet-crazy Gabe", and that a lot of people say puppets are dumb or just for kids. Camp Straight: If it weren't for the fact he shows some interest in Mabel, he could easily be consideredAmbiguously Gaydue to his stereotypically effeminate mannerisms and tone of voice. Chick Magnet: Mabel, Candy, and Grenda fall head over heels for him. Cloudcuckoolander: Very,verypassionate about and obsessed with puppets — to the point of kissing them as if they were living lovers. Even Mabel suddenly realizes she likely dodged a bullet when he rejected her.

characters.name: Marius von Fundshauser
characters.description: A rich teenage Austrian baron who attends the Northwest family's gala in "Northwest Mansion Mystery". 555: Marius' phone number is 555-0176. Amazon Chaser: Ironically, he ends up falling for Grenda due to her aggressive flirting style. Beauty Equals Goodness: His appearance and mannerisms fit this trope. Blue Blood: A baron.Artistic Licenseapplies here, as inReal Life, aristocracy of all kinds is outlawed in Austria ever since the end of World War I, though the titles still exist in Germany.

characters.name: Jeffy Fresh, Byrone, and R-R-Rosie
characters.description: A trio of teenagers who lived in Gravity Falls during the 90s. The online game "Pinesquest" heavily implies that they were killed by the Summerween Trickster after unwittingly creating it. Accidental Murder: Them playing rap music outside Ma and Pa's shop was likely just intended to annoy them, but due to them having nerves of paper, theextremelyinoffensive lyrics end up killing both of them instead. All There in the Manual: The series proper never states their names, or even that they are supposedly dead. Ambiguously Brown: R-R-Rosie. Poke the Poodle: When they were angry about teenagers being banned from the convenience store, they stood outside, danced, and played "shocking" and "offensive" rap music from a boom box.Homework's whack, and so are rules! Tucking in your shirt's for fools!

characters.name: Marcus, Kevin, and Gus Corduroy
characters.description: Wendy's younger brothers who roughhouse with their father, Manly Dan. All There in the Manual: Their names aren't spoken in the show, but are revealed on their character sheets. Eyes Out of Sight: Marcus (the tall one with the hat) has his eyes hidden by his long hair. The only time his eyes have been shown is in a photo of himself and his siblings when they were young. Missing Mom: Theirs and Wendy's mom presumably left their lives after Gus was born.

characters.name: Bus Driver
characters.description: A local Speedy Beaver bus driver who shows up to drive Dipper and Mabel home by the end of the summer. The Cameo: He is voiced byKyle MacLachlan, who starred inTwin Peaks, which was one of the inspirations forGravity Falls. Last Episode, New Character: He arrives at the very end of the show'sGrand Finaleto pick Dipper and Mabel up to bring them home. In fact, he is the last new character in the show. No Name Given: He is only referred to as "Bus Driver" in the credits.

characters.name: Gus Burnside
characters.description: A typical Oregon park ranger that keeps running into mysterious items and situations. He runs the Oregon Parks Department Twitter account. Character Blog: While he primarily tries to post about nature and park info, the account also chronicles the strange things he finds during work. The Faceless: The Twitter account mostly shows pictures from around the park, with the occasional post shot from his perspective. The most he's shown of himself on his own is his arms,and even his missing poster is torn where his face should be. Man on Fire:Heavily implied to be his fate after attempting to burn Bill's book. Bill mentions him by name on the Injury Hotline if the caller chooses getting set on fire as their injury, and if "BURNED INSIDE"notea code itself gotten from typing in "BURNSIDE"is typed into the computer on thisisnotawebsitedotcom.com, a video showing a singed ranger badge and patch being buried plays. Meaningful Name: His last name isBurnside, andhis punishment for burningThe Book of Billis getting set on fire himself.

characters.name: Li'l Gideon
characters.description: The main antagonist of Season 1. Gideon Charles Gleeful, better known by his stage name, Li'l Gideon, is a self-proclaimed televisionpsychic. He owns the Tent of Telepathy and is a competitor of the Mystery Shack. He had one of the journals, and spent the first season trying to destroy the Pines family and the shack, trying to get his hands on the rest of the journals. At the end of the season, he was thwarted, thrown in into prison, and his journal was seized by Stan, but he still plans on escaping. He represents the pentacle on the Zodiac. Abhorrent Admirer: To Mabel. Not that she hates him, she just likes himlike a little sister she can do girly things with,until he tries to kill Dipper. Then she doesn't like himat all. Abusive Offspring: He threatens his parents, leaving his father to accept every single demand and his mother as aNervous Wreck. Alliterative Name:GideonGleeful. Animal Motifs: He’s frequently associated with pigs, due to being porcine and greedy. He has a rather pig-like nose and is known to let out a piggish shriek on occasions where he's in trouble or has been hurt.

characters.name: Agents Powers and Trigger
characters.description: Two agents of avague yet menacing government agencywho come investigating the town's various oddities. Agent Scully: Both of them investigate paranormal occurrences, but have never actually witnessed one.Almost getting eaten by zombies brings them to theAgent Mulderside. Anti-Villain: They'renotbad people by any definition — they're just doing their jobs, and they do have good reason to believe Stan is a dangerous criminal. Of course, we know Stan's not a bad guy, but Powers and Trigger have every right to attempt to arrest him. Arc Villain: Of the first half of Season 2, after Gideon in Season 1, and Bill taking centre stage in the latter half. Big Brother Is Watching: As of "Sock Opera," it's revealed in aFreeze-Frame Bonusthat they've planted listening devices in the Mystery Shack.A live-action interview with Stanreveals that the agency has beenwatching the entire Pines family (on Earth anyway) "for years"and that Powers and Trigger are just an extension of that.

characters.name: Pacifica Elise Northwest
characters.description: The most popular girl in Gravity Falls, and great-great-granddaughter of the town hero Nathaniel Northwest. She represents the llama on the Zodiac. The Ace: Pacifica is very rich, the most popular girl of Gravity Falls, an accomplished mini-golfer, and her family has a long history of doing good deeds.The last one turns out to be a lie. And most of the other stuff is simply a way to please her abusive, selfish, controlling parents. Action Girl: Shows she has promise in "The Golf War" and "Northwest Mansion Mystery". Action Survivor: Nevertheless, she's more able at keeping herself alive when facing the supernatural than actually fighting it.She's also one of the few citizens who manages to avoid being captured by Bill and is part of Stan's army. All Girls Like Ponies: In "Weirdmageddon 3", she is seen reading a magazine called "Pony Fancy".When Preston Northwest is forced to sell their mansion to uphold their family's wealth, Priscilla tearfully informs her daughter that she will only be able to keep one pony from now on - much to Pacifica's dismay.

characters.name: Preston Northwest
characters.description: The main antagonist of "Northwest Mansion Mystery". He is Pacifica's father and patriarch of the Northwest family, the founder of Gravity Falls. Arichandpublicly lovedfigure for the town, he shows immense disdain for the poor and everyone beneath him. Abusive Dad: Is all-but-stated in "The Golf War" to emotionally abuse Pacifica. "Northwest Mansion Mystery" reveals that he has used Pavlovian conditioning on her, training her to meekly back down from opposing him at the sound of a bell. Apocalypse Cult: If that picture ofBill Cipher being worshipped in the Northwest house is any indication, not to mention his immediate response to Bill's arrival being offering to join him.It turns out thatAbigale Northwest (maiden name Blackwing) is linked to Silas Birchtree through her being a member of the Anti-Cipher Society, which explains the amount of Bill-related paraphernalia within the mansion. It turns out thatAbigale Northwest (maiden name Blackwing) is linked to Silas Birchtree through her being a member of the Anti-Cipher Society, which explains the amount of Bill-related paraphernalia within the mansion. Archnemesis Dad: Though Pacifica doesn't always view him as such, his constant abuse towards her makes him something of an opponent to her.This is part of the reason why she finally stood up to him.

characters.name: Priscilla Northwest
characters.description: Preston's wife and Pacifica's mother. Abusive Mom: She's just as psychologically and emotionally abusive towards her daughter as her husband, having hammered the idea that appearances areeverythinginto her head from a very young age. Break the Haughty:Seeing the Northwest Mansion being sold off thanks to her husband Preston clearly devastated her. Control Freak: She's overly fussy and demanding with Pacifica's attire and mannerisms.What did I tell you about that dress? The theme issea foamgreen, not lake foam green! Go change! Happy Marriage Charade: Pacifica’s story in thisisnotawebsitecom strongly suggests that Priscilla isn’t happy with Preston despite appearances, with subtext that she cheated andPacifica isn't his daughter.

characters.name: Nathaniel Northwest
characters.description: The 19th century frontiersman who founded Gravity Falls. 0% Approval Rating: Even before his rise to power, he was already a dimwit who only knew how to shovel horse manure that people really couldn't have cared less about. His approval from the lumberjacks quickly fell apart once he revealed that he tricked them and went back on his word, and his hostile and jerkish behavior towards the locals made them all loathe him. By the time he was finally gone after stupidly thinking he could eat oak bark to prove himself as a wizard, absolutely no one tried to help, nor did they miss or mourn him afterward. Alliterative Name:NathanielNorthwest. Ambiguous Situation: It's hard to say if the statements about him wereBased on a Great Big Lie,Obfuscating StupidityorSanity Slippagefrom long after he inherited his title. Asshole Victim: A horrible monster of a human being who was ultimately killed after he went crazy, and inattempting to eat a tree to prove he was a wizard, choked to death on a piece of bark. Nobody shed a tear.

characters.name: Robbie Stacey Valentino
characters.description: A friend of Wendy's, and a former rival of Dipper's for her affection. He is currently dating Tambry. He represents the stitched heart on the Zodiac. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: His parents are incredibly cheerful and upbeat, albeit with a morbid sense of humor befitting their jobs as funeral directors. Bad Liar: Manipulative, certainly, but he's terrible at actual deception.Robbie:SoI was attacked by this magic kung-fu guythat was throwing, like, balls of FIRE at me...[Proudly]I kicked his butt, though.Blind Ivan:[Clearly exasperated]Robbie, speak HONESTLY.Robbie:[Ashamed]...I was saved by a 12-year-old.Taken to ridiculous extremes in "The Love God". After Wendy and her friends hear a brief snippet of a song he wrote about their breakup, he claims that it was written about another girl named Wendy. Nobody believes him for a second. Taken to ridiculous extremes in "The Love God". After Wendy and her friends hear a brief snippet of a song he wrote about their breakup, he claims that it was written about another girl named Wendy. Nobody believes him for a second. Belligerent Sexual Tension:With Tambry. Even before Mabel brought out the love potion, you could tell there wassomethingthere.

characters.name: Blendin Blandin
characters.description: Blendin Blenjamin Blandin is a time traveler who was sent two hundred andsñeventhousand years into the past to stop a series of time anomalies that were supposed to happen during the Mystery Fair. Actor Allusion: Justin Roiland uses the exact same voice asMortyfor Blendin, right down to the occasional stammering, and even says "Aw, geez" in "Blendin's Game". All for Nothing:Blendin hoped that Dipper and Mabel would decode the secret message he wrote in the 1800s. Sadly, the twins never decoded the message and were thrown into the bottomless pit along with the journals. Ultimately, Blendin's attempt to contact Dipper and Mabel was all in vain. Alliterative Name:BlendinBlandin. It borders on aRepetitive Name. Bald of Evil: Not a single hair on his head.Near the end of "Blendin's Game", however, the twins grant him some hair in addition to his job back.

characters.name: The Gnomes
characters.description: The little men of the Gravity Falls forest. Adorable Evil Minions: Let's face it: the gnomes are pretty cute. Aerith and Bob: Parodied. The five gnomeswho make up Normanare named Jeff, Carson, Jason, Steve, and Shmebulock. Affably Evil: Jeff is very friendly and personable, but still tries toforce a twelve-year old girl to marry thousandswithout regret. He was also planning oneating Steveif he didn't get any pie. All of the Other Reindeer: According toLost Legends, the other gnomes don't think too highly of Shmebulock due to hisPokémon Speakcondition.

characters.name: Bud and Mrs. Gleeful
characters.description: The parents of Gideon Charles Gleeful. Bud runs a used car lot right behind the family's house. Mrs. Gleeful is a stay-at-home mother. Affably Evil: Bud, as evidenced by the picture of Stan on his (and/or Gideon's)Dartboard of Hate.There is also his membership in the Society of the Blind Eye. Ancient Conspiracy: Bud is a member ofthe Society of the Blind Eye. Awful Wedded Life: In the (dubiously canon) coloring bookGravity Falls: Don't Color This Book! It's Cursed!, one of Mabel's matchmaking projects is Mrs. Gleeful and Farmer Sprott, on the basis that the former seems like the type to read bodice-rippers that involve the protagonist leaving her husband for a farmer. Badass Boast: Bud gives one to Stan Pines when he ran against him in "The Stanchurian Candidate".Bud: I was gonna let bygones be bygones, Stan, but you just made apowerfulenemy. I'll win either way, and when I do you may not like the Gravity Falls you wake up in!

characters.name: Ghost Eyes
characters.description: A local inmate who becomes the second-in-command of Gideon's prison gang. Affably Evil: He's a convict, but he's a true friend to Gideon, even consoling him when one of Gideon's schemes falls apart. Blood Knight: He and the other convicts lose focus on the twins and assist Gideon inopposing Bill Cipher. Partly due toUndying Loyalty, partly due to excitement at fighting a "chaos god". Bruiser with a Soft Center: Acts this way toward Gideon, whom he's very gentle toward. The Brute: Becomes Gideon's main muscle.

characters.name: Bill's Henchmaniacs
characters.description: Bill's fellow demons and monsters from the Nightmare Realm, who wish to wreak havoc across Earth along with him. All Love Is Unrequited: According to Bill, 8-Ball is completely in love with Pyronica, but he always gets burned. Whether he means this figuratively orvery literallyis anyone's guess. All There in the Manual: The Lava Lamp creature's name is "Lava Lamp Guy" as revealed in a deleted scene from "Weirdmageddon 2: Escape from Reality". Anthropomorphic Food: Zanthar is a giant, purple loaf of bread with four ape-like legs. Army of Thieves and Whores: Bill calls them "the gang of interdimensional criminals and nightmares I call my friends!"

characters.name: The Beasts
characters.description: A trio of monstrous beings that have stolen the gemulets from the Gnome Kingdom for some unknown nefarious purpose. Jeff assigns Dipper and Mabel the task of retrieving the gemulets from these foul creatures. Berserk Button: The Fire Beast reacts poorly to hisExposition Dumpbeing compared to the plot of a '90s animated movie. Brought Down to Normal: Parodied.When Dipper asks the Fire Beast for his help in battling Dark Jeff, the Beast turns him down, saying that he is weak without his powers. Never mind that even without the Gemulets, the Beasts are still hulking minotaurs that look like they could snap a grown man in half like a twig. Good All Along:The player is led to believe that The Beasts are wicked evildoers, when in fact they are peaceful guardians who are trying to prevent Gravity Falls from descending into darkness once more. The Fire Beast in particular is quite the affable fellow. The Quiet One: It is initially unclear whether they are evencapableof speech.During his meeting with Dipper and Mabel in the midst of Dark Jeff's reign, the Fire Beast turns out to be rather talkative and friendly. He claims that he simply has a tendency to go into a "blind, incoherent rage" when protecting the gemulets. What the excuse is for the other Beasts is unclear.

characters.name: The Gravity Falls Gobblewonker
characters.description: The Gobblewonker is a legendary sea monster that is thought to live at the bottom of Lake Gravity Falls. Back for the Finale:Its head and neck become the tail for the Shack-tron during Weirdmageddon. Mechanical Monster:The Gobblewonker turns out to have been a robot built by Old ManMcGucket. Monster of the Week: Of "The Legend of the Gobblewonker". Not the Nessie: Rathera robot made byMcGucket.

characters.name: The Mystery Shack Wax Statue Collection
characters.description: The Wax figures are living wax sculptures that Grunkle Stan stole from a garage sale and used as attractions in the Mystery Shack. Affably Evil: Wax Larry King. As Himself: Both the Coolio and Larry King wax figures actually are actually voiced by the real Coolio and Larry King. Due in part to this, some of the lines given to Larry King were written just to see if he'd say them. Back for the Finale: Wax Larry King's disembodied head has a cameo in the final episode — and he's still stuck inside the duct. At least until he becomes the top of a flagpole. Blank White Eyes: Invoked when they go on the offensive after revealing themselves. They all roll their eyes to the backs of their heads to menacingly present blank whites to the Mystery Shack residents. This does nothing to impair their vision.

characters.name: Smile Dip Dogs
characters.description: Two yellow dogs that Mabel sees after eating way too much Smile Dip, a hallucinogenic candy. One has a purple collar and is called "the Beast," while the other has a purple bowtie. A Beast in Name and Nature: InThe Book of Bill, the left one is referred to simply as "the Beast" by the Theraprism counselors. Bright Is Not Good: They’re bright yellow cartoon dogs, but according to the Theraprism staff, the left one (at least) is as dangerous asBill Cipher. The Cameo: InThe Book of Bill, the Beast appears on the list of Theraprism inmates. Higher Understanding Through Drugs: Mabel can only see and interact with them after eating an absurd amount of Smile Dip.

characters.name: Pa and Ma Duskerton
characters.description: The ghosts of an old married couple who ran and died in the now-abandoned Dusk 2 Dawn convenience store. Affably Evil: They're such a sweet, old couple that you could easily forget that they're also vengeful and sadistic spirits who inflict horrible punishments on the teenagers who broke into their haunting grounds. Berserk Button: Theyreallydon't like teenagers. Big "NO!": When they were alive, they banned teenagers from their store, but three teens protested by dancing and playing "shocking" and "offensive" rap music outside ("Homework's whack, and so are rules! Tucking in your shirt's for fools!"). Pa Duskerton went "Nooooooooo!" before he and his wife promptly died of double heart attacks. Domain Holder: Inside the abandoned convenience store, they're basically omnipotent and can warp reality inside the store as much as they please.

characters.name: The Manotaurs
characters.description: A species of half man, half minotaur creatures who reside in the mountains.Emphasis on man. Abhorrent Alpha Male: They're are a group of ultra-buff hypermasculine minotaurs who embody stereotypes about masculinity to a toxic extent, with Dipper's encounter with them serving as a metaphor for puberty with the moral that being a man doesn’t mean having to be rude, cruel, or violent. Alien Blood: They have green-colored blood, as shown when Leaderaur pulls a spear out of his chest. Always Someone Better: Downplayed and played for laughs; the manotaurs are so ferociously, impossibly manly that even Manly Dan, the single-most macho manly he-man resident of Gravity Falls, is afraid of them. When Chutzpar, the first manotaur, is about to arrive on the scene, Manly Dan is shown fleeing in terror, shouting a warning at Dipper to run for his life as he goes. Ambiguously Jewish: Chutzpar has sidelocks reminiscent of Orthodox Jews, what looks like a skull cap, and his name is a portmanteau of "chutzpah" (Yiddish/Hebrew for audacity) and "par" (Hebrew for bull).

characters.name: The Multi-Bear
characters.description: The Multi-Bear is a magical beast that lives in the Multi-Bear's cave at the top of a high mountain. Back for the Finale:He appears along with several other characters we haven't seen in a while at the end of "Weirdmageddon Part 2". Bears Are Bad News: Subverted. It turns out the Multi-Bear isn't really a bad guy. Beary Friendly: He's actually quite nice. Commonality Connection: He's a huge fan of BABBA, the same girly pop band that made Dipper go on his quest for manliness. Upon bonding over this, Dipper can't find the will to hurt him.

characters.name: The Photocopy Clones
characters.description: The clones are copies of Dipper, made from Stan's copy machine. Affably Evil: When they rise up against Dipper Classic, they just lock him in the closet with snacks, showing no desire to actually hurt him. All There in the Script: According toGravity Falls: Journal 3,Dippers #3 and #4 go by Tracey and Quattro, respectively. Alternative-Self Name-Change: Most of them go by their clone number. The first clone, while marked as #2, goes by Tyrone instead due to the implications of #2. As established inGravity Falls: Journal 3, Dippers #3 and #4 later start calling themselves Tracey and Quattro. Then there is Paper Jam Dipper. Anti-Mutiny:The clone Dippers betray the real Dipper because he wanted to abandon their ridiculously detailed plan and just talk to Wendy directly. When #2 realizes that the original plan wasn't working, they laugh it off and share a soda instead.

characters.name: Quentin Trembley
characters.description: Sir Lord Quentin Trembley III, Esq., is a mysterious figure involved in the many riddles of Gravity Falls and America itself. Babies Make Everything Better: Averted. He appointed six babies to the Supreme Court, which contributed to his deposal and replacement. Back for the Finale: Appears in the credit montage for the finale, where we see that Trembley is still exploring the forests of Gravity Falls on his horse. Still not wearing pants. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: For all his eccentricities, Trembley is a brilliant man. The Caligula: Elected by a landslide (as in the other candidates were literally buried by one), he proceeded to ban pants, declare war on pancakes, andappoint babies to the Supreme Court. He was eventually deposed, replaced byWilliam Henry Harrison, andall evidence of his term stricken from the national record. He ended upfounding Gravity Falls, being deposedagainand finally encasing himself in peanut brittle,in an attempt to live forever— which, amazingly enough, worked.

characters.name: Time Baby
characters.description: A giant, time-devouring, baby-like monster currently frozen in Antarctica. For unknown reasons, he will wage a war in the distant future, while also leading human time travelers to fix timeline anomalies. All There in the Manual:The Book of Billreveals that his real name is Chronelius Infinitium Titanicus the Infinitieth. Always a Bigger Fish: A fairly unorthodox example. InDipper's and Mabel's Guide to Mystery and Nonstop Fun!, Bill Cipher claims that Time Baby is an even worse entity than he is. That same book has a coded message that says that even in a future where he reigns supreme, Time Baby is "worried about Bill".As a sign of just how powerful Bill has become upon gaining physical form, he completely destroys Time Baby in "Weirdmageddon Part 1". Althoughhe'll regenerate eventually. Anti-Villain: Time Baby may be a tyrant, but everything he does is to protect the universe and ensure the space-time continuum works properly. If you get on his good side, he proves to be a valuable yet powerful ally. He certainly didn't mind helping out the heroes on Blendin's request. Bad Boss: Implied to be this. When Blendin Blandin failed his mission, he was afraid of Time Baby and begged him for mercy.

characters.name: RumbleMcSkirmish
characters.description: RumbleMcSkirmishis a playable fighter in an arcade game calledFight Fighters. Dipper brought him into the real world by using the ultimate power code that he found on the lower left side of the arcade game. AcCENT upon the Wrong SylLABle: Rumble talks like this all the time. Always a Bigger Fish: After his initial appearance, he's on the receiving end ofTWOof these, once by.GIFfanywhen she temporarily passes through his arcade machine and casually curbstomps him, and once again in the finale, where he is once again out in the real world, and finds that all his fighting skills are useless against Bill Cipher. Ambidextrous Sprite: As befitting a 2DFighting Gamecharacter pastiche, his eyepatch changes sides based on the direction he's facing. Lampshaded by Dipper inJournal 3. Anti-Air:During the fight against the fight against the Henchmaniacs, Rumble basically acts as an Anti-Air cannon for the Mystery Shack, flingingfireballsat anything that flies too close.

characters.name: The Summerween Trickster
characters.description: The Summerween Trickster is a large, light purple monster with a yellow-green jack-o-lantern mask and the first monster to actually pose a serious threat to the twins' lives. Ax-Crazy:He eats children. Berserk Button: Don't "lack Summerween spirit" near this guy.Don't throw candy in the trash, either. Child Eater: If Dipper, Mabel, Grenda and Candy fail to meet his candy quota for the night, he'll eat them. Child Hater: The Summerween Trickster is clearly bitter towardsallchildren as a result of never being eaten - it’s claimed that he only goes after the children who lack Summerween spirit, but if that’s true, he would’ve ignored Gorney (who is clearly all for Summerween).

characters.name: The Gremloblin
characters.description: A giant, rampaging beast, with the ability to show a person their worst nightmare. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: Gets distracted by a novelty rubber singing fish for an indeterminate amount of time. Generation Xerox:When his evil eye is turned on him, he sees his worst fear, himself in a mirror with glasses telling him that he's turned into his father. Glowing Eyes of Doom: Has big, glowing yellow eyes that can drive you clinically insane if you look into them. Hoist by His Own Petard: When his eye is turned on himhe sees himself as his father, and he runs off screaming.

characters.name: Tumbleweed Terror Pinball Game
characters.description: A pinball game with aWild Westtheme and a sentient, talking cowboy skull. When Soos gets the high score by tilting with Dipper and Mabel's help, the skull sucks them into the game. Achilles' Heel: The main power switch. Not only shuts down the entire system, but it also releases those trapped. Berserk Button: Hates being tilted. As a pinball machine, his whole world is pinball, so he's not too happy when you mess with his only purpose. Glowing Eyes of Doom: The cowboy skull has glowing eyes, and it tries to kill the main characters for tilting the pinball machine/ No Fair Cheating: Punishes tilting by sucking the offenders into the game andkilling them.

characters.name: Mermando
characters.description: A young Latino (likely Mexican) merman who winds up trapped in Gravity Falls public pool. Luckily Mabel befriends him and helps break him out. Arranged Marriage: In "Society of the Blind Eye", Mermando sends to Mabel the news of his arranged marriage to the queen of manatees, in order to prevent a revolt in the sea. Artists Are Attractive: Mabel says, "and you can play at least one chord on the guitar" to him after telling him that he's the coolest guy she's ever met. Bathtub Mermaid: Mermando can't breathe without water, so Mabel ends up transporting him in a cooler. Blue Blood: Implied. He seems to be a merman prince if he was able to get married to the manatee queen in order to prevent a revolt.

characters.name: Sev'ral Timez
characters.description: A good looking, astonishingly dimBoy Bandmade up of clones. Its members are Greggy C, Creggy G, Leggy P, Chubby Z, and Deep Chris. Animal Motifs: Hamsters, which fits with their characterization as aBoy Bandwhose members are trained to perform for others. Their manager keeps them in a giant hamster cage and they tend to act like hamsters on occasion.In the finale, they even power the Shacktron byrunning on a treadmill. Back for the Finale:They take part in the assault on Bill's Fearamid by helping build the Shacktron, and then running on a treadmill (spurred on by a dangling piece of meat) to provide it with extra power. Born in the Wrong Century: Downplayed: Dipper describes them as "the boy-band that came a decade too late". Boy Band: Your typical band made up of fivePretty Boysthat have a ton of screaming fangirls. Also parodied, since any jokes about how boy bands are "manufactured" by the music industry are quite literal in their case due to being clones, and their stereotypical overbearing manager keeps them in a giant hamster cage and verbally abuses them.

characters.name: The Pterodactyl
characters.description: A prehistoric beast, unleashed on Gravity Falls after millions of years of being suspended in tree sap. All Flyers Are Birds: Shrieks like a hawk, has eagle-like feet, and makes chicken-like nests. At least it's a quadruped. Ambiguous Gender: It has eggs, and seeing as there's no sign of another pterodactyl in the area, we can assume at first that it laid the eggs, which would designate it as a female. However, it's consistently referred to by male pronouns and has a large crest akin to a male pterosaur, and seeing as some of the other prehistoric creatures thawed out offscreen, it's possible that its mate did too and we just didn't see it. Animals Not to Scale: It most closely resemblesPteranodon, but it's gigantic, large enough for a grown man and a pig to ride on.In some shots, it appears larger than the largest known pterosaurs. Artistic License – Paleontology: Looks like an unholy mixture of all stereotypes, down to the scaly skin, being called a "dinosaur" (thoughStanfordcorrectly identifies it as a "pterosaur" in Journal 3), having eagle-like hindlimbs, leathery wings, having aPteranodoncrest alongside rather mismatched teeth (which makes it coincidentally resembleLudodactylus), making chicken-like nests andhaving zero to no body fat. Strangely enough, though, it is quadrupedal like a real pterosaur. Ford lampshades these in the 3rd journal, even noting that it doesn’t match any known pterosaur in the fossil record.

characters.name: Xyler and Craz
characters.description: Two '80s style boys from the movie Dream Boy High. Mabel appears to have a crush on them. They were brought to life by Mabel's imagination. '80s Hair: It goes well with their entire appearance, which comes from an '80s movie. All There in the Manual: Their surnames are revealed inThe Book of Bill(Xyler's is Q. Blaze while Craz's is Zazzler). Anti-Nihilist:Upon realizing they can exist outside of Mabel's mind or herLotus-Eater Machine, they have a bit of an existential crisis. They promptly decide it's actually rather radical. Art Shift: During their part of Mabel's fantasy, the backgrounds are rendered to resemblethe painted cels of an 80s cartoonrather thanGravity Falls's usual style.

characters.name: Candy Monster
characters.description: A short and hairy humanoid monster who tried to steal Dipper and Mabel's Summerween candy. Abnormal Ammo: At one point, he resorts to throwing the candy he's eating at Dipper. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: Was stopped when Dipper distracted him with a television. Big Eater: Not even a golf club was spared from his hunger. Expy: Bares quite a resemblance to Krumm fromAaahh!!! Real Monsters, with his gross hairy nakedness and prominent eyes.

characters.name: The Mailbox
characters.description: A mysterious mailbox in the middle of the forest that can answer any questions asked of it. The Omniscient: Can answer any question placed inside it. Self-Destruct Mechanism: The mailbox destroys itself when Mabel places a video of her shoving gummy worms up her nose. Story-Breaker Power: Given that its omniscience meant it could answer literallyanyquestion, including the identity of the journal's author,you HAD to figurethat something or someone would intervene to prevent it from revealing one of the big plot points of Season 2. Cue Mabel and her gummy worms video offending it enough to trigger a self-destruct.

characters.name: Lefty
characters.description: A resident in Gravity Falls who works at the bowling alley, and for some reason is always facing left. Cyanide Pill:When Lefty's secret is revealed, the aliens controlling him commit suicide by swallowing glowing cubes that cause them to drop dead,then their corpses explode. Killed Off for Real:When the aliens piloting him are exposed, they all take their suicide cubes, and Lefty himself bursts into flames. Leaning on the Fourth Wall: Let's face it, Lefty's entire schtick(that he's actually a robot piloted by aliens, and he is only looking left because his right side's nonexistence would be exposed)is only possible in a 2D cartoon. Mobile-Suit Human:Turns out to be one controlled by a bunch of tiny aliens.

characters.name: Hide Behind
characters.description: A tall and skinny creature that hides behind people. Ambiguously Evil: It has a frightening appearance and is shown sneaking up behind Dipper, but it's not clear if it has any sort of actual motive. Fearsome Critters: The Hide-Behind is based on a creature from American folklore, though the one from the stories is a bear-like creature that sucks in its stomach to hide behind things. He Who Must Not Be Seen:Invoked. As indicated in its name, the Hide Behind is rarely, if ever, actually seen by anyone. Lean and Mean: Though he appears to be more mischievous than malicious.

characters.name: Island Head Beast
characters.description: The origin of a giant human tooth found on the shores of the Gravity Falls Lake. Is in fact a giant floating head with an island growing on it, which sleeps in the lake and goes after Mabel and Dipper when they "disturb its slumber." Black Speech: Its speech is reversed, creating the impression of this. Oracular Head: Of gigantic proportions. Our Monsters Are Weird: A sentient, bodyless thing the size of a small lake island. That's No Moon: That little island in the lake? It's not an island...

characters.name: Octavia
characters.description: A mutant cow on display at the Gravity Falls Petting Zoo. Has five extra legs due to the pollution caused by a mud flap factory's runoff. Ascended to Carnivorism:Her mutation has apparently given her a taste for meat, since immediately after being freed she shoots a bird out of the sky with herEye Beamsand starts eating it. Back for the Finale:Appears in a cameo near the end of the last episode as one of the creatures waving Dipper and Mabel goodbye. Body Horror: Three of her extra legs are growing out of her back, with another growing out of each side. Eye Beams: Thanks, radioactive material!

characters.name: The Zombie Horde
characters.description: A group of zombies summoned by Dipper, while trying to demonstrate the journal's power. Alien Blood: It glows green. Connected All Along: It is strongly implied in theJournal 3that they are the reanimated corpses of the lumberjacks killed by the mudslide of the episode "Northwest Mansion Mystery", being washed down to the land in which the Mystery Shack was eventually built — hence why the shack had so many dead bodies buried on its surroundings. Glowing Eyes of Doom: Their eyes glow green as well. It Can Think: They're generally mindless and savage, to the point that zombified Soos is considered a genius among them, but they show a few hints of intelligence. When zombie Soos gets distracted by a television show, another zombie grunts in annoyance at him. They are also visibly confused when Dipper, Mabel, and Stan start singing karaoke at them (one even does aQuizzical Tilt).

characters.name: Experiment 210/The Shape Shifter
characters.description: A monstrous shape-changer discovered in the author's underground bunker. Alas, Poor Villain: In Journal 3, the Author was genuinely sad to have him locked away, though it didn't stop him in the end — particularly given what Shifty had just done to his assistant. Alien Blood: It's green. Ax-Crazy: Tries to murder four innocent people just so he could steal the journal. Ironically, he got slashed by an axe as part of his defeat. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He uses his shape-shifting powers to deceive Dipper and Wendy by impersonating the Author.

characters.name: The Liliputtians
characters.description: Tiny creatures who inhabit the local mini-golf course at "Ye Olde Discount Putt Hutt", and fight over whose hole is the best. Affably Evil: Being voiced by Patton Oswalt naturally leads to Franz sounding quite friendly, no matter what he's doing. As Long as It Sounds Foreign:Played for Laughswith the French lilliputtian. His dialogue is literally just stereotypical French phrases completely unrelated to his subtitles. Ax-Crazy: The little bastards are a tad bit unhinged. Cute and Psycho: They're small and adorable, but will go to any length to get what they want. They tried to shred Pacifica to get Mabel's sticker, and when she eats it, they decide to cut her open to get it.

characters.name: Bipper
characters.description: Bill Cipher's mind in Dipper's body. Achilles' Heel: Bipper's main drawback is that Bill no longer harbors the abilities of anEnergy Beingand instead has the strength of a preteen boy. All There in the Manual: Thepublished Journal 3reveals that, had Bill succeeded, he would have thrown Dipper's body off the water tower, making it look like Dipper went crazy and committed suicide, while leaving the real Dipper trapped as a mindscape-ghost forever. Deal with the Devil: Bill needs consent to possess someone, so the only way Bipper can come into existence is if Bill and Dipper shake hands on the matter. That said, as long as Bill worded the deal right, he can get by this by tricking Dipper into thinking he just wants to use one of Mabel's sock puppets. Demonic Possession: He's the body of Dipper Pines while being possessed by the dream demon Bill.

characters.name: .GIFfany
characters.description: The love interest of the JapaneseDating SimgameRomance Academy 7. Also happens to be sentient, andrather possessiveof her player. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: She reveals that in the past, her developers found out that something was gravely wrong with her and tried to delete her.She deleted them instead. Always a Bigger Fish: Blasted Rumble while in his arcade game. Animesque: Her overall design is very obviously meant to mimic an anime style.JustifiedsinceIn-Universe, she's a character from a JapaneseDating Sim. Badass Adorable: She can possess and poweranythingelectronic, gaining complete control over it. This control is demonstrated to Rumble as he tries to fight.GIFfanywhile she passes through his arcade game, she casually oneshots him and moves along.

characters.name: Hand Witch
characters.description: An ugly witch who steals peoples' hands, including Stan's when he insults her and steals one of her golden watches. Abhorrent Admirer: Her look as an old hag and her lack of charisma made her one to both Stan andFord. Her prospects start looking up after Mabel gives her a book of Dating Advice. Canon Immigrant: The special she appeared in was not canon, but her existence apparently is, as she appeared inGravity Falls: Journal 3andGravity Falls: Lost Legends. Department of Redundancy Department: According to the swap meet pamphlet, the Hand Witch lives in a horrible Hand Witch lair on Hand Witch Mountain.Stan:Stop saying Hand Witch! Familiar: Has dozens of disembodied hands at her disposal.

characters.name: Claymation Monsters
characters.description: Animated monsters that were brought to life by Harry Claymore through black magic. Medium Blending: Made with actual stop motion animation courtesy ofStoopid Buddy Studios. Non-Standard Character Design: As they are actually stop motion animation. Shout-Out: To monsters inRay Harryhausenfilms likeJason and the Argonauts. Start of Darkness: CGI animation replacing stop motion is why they turned evil.

characters.name: Society of the Blind Eye
characters.description: A secret society that works to keep the abnormalities of Gravity Falls secret. They are led by Blind Ivan. Ancient Conspiracy: Well, not that ancient, but it IS a conspiracy to keep things hidden in Gravity Falls. Bald of Evil: Blind Ivan, whose baldness shows a scalp covered in tattoos. Connected All Along:Turns outMcGucketmet Blind Ivan (then known as Ivan Wexler) when the latter was a teen working at a carnival. The Dog Was the Mastermind:The leader is an unknown, but the rest of the society is filled out by minor and joke characters. Unknown to all of the members (due to their own memory wipes, no less), their revered founder is FiddlefordMcGucket.

characters.name: Love God
characters.description: A cherub/cupid who moonlights as a rock star. Ambiguously Bi: We see him get out of the back of a van with a woman and Tyler, both of whom he calls "groupies". Apologetic Attacker: He apologizes twice when he uses the visions of heartbreak past"Sorry, Kids, but you've left me no choice. Visions of heartbreak past!" Beware the Nice Ones: If he thinks you're interfering with his job, he'll show some of the nastier applications ofThe Power of Love—like summoning visions of your past heartbreaks to manipulate you. Big Beautiful Man:In-Universe, at least. Cupid is popular enough to pull offA Lady on Each Arm.

characters.name: Ghost of Northwest Manor/Lumberjack Ghost
characters.description: A powerful and dangerous ghost haunting the Northwest's manor. Ambiguously Related:Journal 3 reveals his name to be Archibald Corduroy, and he resembles Wendy's father Manly Dan Corduroy, who alsohappens to be a lumberjack. All this heavily implies he is related to Wendy, but it's unclear if it's through his child or a sibling if he is. Anti-Villain: He hasmore than a legitimategrievance against the Northwest family, his problem ispoor impulse controland a tendency towards collateral damage. Ax-Crazy: Dipper describes him as "unstable", and he fits this perfectly, happy to murder dozens of innocent people in his quest for vengeance against the Northwest family. To top it all off, heliterallyhas an axe that was stuck on his head. Bald of Evil: He'd lost all the hair on the top of his head by the time he met Nathaniel Northwest, which carries on upon his return as a ghost.

characters.name: Cycloptopus
characters.description: A one-eyed octopus-like creature that escaped from the basement. Ax-Crazy: This thing is pretty violent. Cyclops: Has only one eye Our Monsters Are Weird: Certainly not something you'd encounter in everyday life, especially something whose eye turns into its mouth. Shout-Out: It looks suspiciously similar toShuma-Gorath.

characters.name: Probabilitor the Annoying
characters.description: The mascot of "Dungeons, Dungeons & More Dungeons" summoned from another dimension by the Infinity Die. Affably Evil: Although he is a villain and wants to eat Dipper andFord's brains, he genuinely enjoys playing DD&MD and tells Stan that the game is fun. He also plays by the rules while choosing a game edition that's to his advantage. Art Evolution: In-universe example; as Dipper notes, the creators ofDD&MDlike to change Probabilitor's appearance every few years. Unfortunately, this led to anAudience-Alienating Erain the 1990s (see below).invoked Basement Dweller: If his mom is making him his lunch is any indication. Brain Food: He plans to eatGrunkle Fordand Dipper's to increase his "in-chant-elligence".

characters.name: Celestabellebethabelle
characters.description: A unicorn whose hair is needed to Bill-proof the shack. Absurdicorn: Celestabellebethabelle is a unicorn whose hair is needed to Bill-proof the shack. She refuses to offer a single strand because she claims Mabel is a bad person. The rest of Mabel's squad conspires to steal the hair anyway, and Mabel attempts to stop them. Some other Unicorns come in and say that Unicorns can't determine pure-heartedness, and that C-Beth is just a douchebag who wants to be left alone. Action Figure Speech: When speaking, her horn glows, but she never moves her mouth. Alien Blood:When Mabel decks her, shebleedsrainbow. Back for the Finale:She's part of Stan's army during Weirdmageddon.

characters.name: Darlene
characters.description: Stan's biggest rival tourist trap owner, and secretly a spider creature who uses the place to draw her victims. Achilles' Heel: Anything that takes care of normal spiders works on her if it's big enough. Black Widow: To an almost literal extent. She seduces men and kills them afterwards, though her motivation isfoodrather than money. Dead Guy on Display: Darlene's MO is displaying the corpses of her victimsin plain sightas a mummy attraction. Giant Spider: Her true form, though she usually keeps her top half human to make it even more unsettling.

characters.name: Crash Site Omega Security Droids
characters.description: A pair of robotic spheres that activate when Dipper and Ford accidentally trigger the UFO's ancient security system. Killer Robot: They show the signs of this. They cannot be reasoned with, nor do they hesitate to try to capture Dipper and Ford. Monster of the Week: Of "Dipper and Mabel vs. the Future", and the final ones encountered in the series. Silent Antagonist: Neither of them speaks and only lets out creepy humming sounds.

characters.name: The Horrifying, Sweaty, One-Armed Monstrosity
characters.description: A massive human head with an arm growing out of its top and no body, who wanders Gravity Falls trying to eat people. Affably Evil: He's strangely direct about wanting to eat people, and seems to take no for an answer during the credits. Dipper's "rudeness" in trying to escape and ignoring him bothered him more than anything else. Cephalothorax: With no body parts besides a head and an arm growing out of its top, he qualifies. Even Bad Men Love Their Mamas: He's a human-eating monster, but when disappointed, he plans to call his mother. Ineffectual Sympathetic Villain: His pathetic attempts to get someone to go in his mouth make it hard to hate him.

characters.name: Mabeland
characters.description: Bill Cipher's most diabolical trap, where he placed Mabel after starting Weirdmageddon. The bubble creates whatever its tenants want the most, and since this is Mabel, it's the most zany place of all. Natives include Dippy-Fresh, a 'cooler' version of Dipper who likes skateboarding and supporting his sister, and Judge Kitty Kitty Meow Meow Face Schwartzstein, who presides over the trial of Fantasy vs Reality, and, well, every other crazy thing Mabel's imagined. Ambiguously Jewish: Played for laughs, as the Judge'sOverly Long Nameends inSchwartzstein,in reference to his Jewish voice actor. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: The Judge gets distracted by a string of yarn before the Fantasy vs. Reality court case. Berserk Button: They hate reality so much that they'll attack anyone, even Mabel. Cloud Cuckoolander: The Judge, due to being part of Mabelworld.

characters.name: Hawkers
characters.description: WingedMookswho serve the Beasts. Airborne Mook: They possess wings and attack from above. Animate Inanimate Object: These things are the living top parts of a totem. Brainwashed and Crazy:Just like the Totems, they also gets wind up by Dark Jeff's Magical powers at the second half of the game. Good All Along:They were only serving the Beasts in their duty to guard the gemulets.

characters.name: Totems
characters.description: Mooks who serve the Beasts. Alongside the Hawkers, they serve as the main non-boss enemies inGravity Falls: Legend of the Gnome Gemulets. They come in types: the Creeping Totems, who patrol the woodland floor, and the stationary Flaming Totems. Animate Inanimate Object: The Journal describes the Flaming Totems as living campfires, while the Creeping Totems are said to be "cursed wood carvings". Brainwashed and Crazy:In the back half of the game, they wind up under the influence of Dark Jeff's magical powers. Good All Along:Like the Hawkers, they were merely serving their masters in an ultimately benevolent cause. Mix-and-Match Critters: The Creeping Totems' faces are clearly meant to be reminiscent of squirrels, while their legs appear to be tentacles like those on a cephalopod.

characters.name: Mr. What's-His-Face
characters.description: A shadowy, face-stealing monster Pacifica summoned in an ill-advised attempt to get rid of facial wrinkles. The Blank: True to his purpose, he lacks a face, outside of a huge mouth of teeth, including a gold tooth to the right of the center. Exact Words: Guarantees Pacifica a face that's "completely blemish free". Face Stealer: Takes people's (still-living, talking) faces for its private collection. Shadowed Face, Glowing Eyes:Replace eyes with mouthand that's this guy's whole design in a nutshell.

characters.name: Cursed Comic Books
characters.description: A pile of comic books given sapience and magic power when shoved into Stanford's cursed chest. Insistent Terminology: Insisting on the term "graphic novel" over "comics", and willattack anyone over that alone. Trapped in TV Land: Can suck people into any of the comic books it's made of.

characters.name: Alternate Mabels
characters.description: A collection of alternate-dimension Mabels that fell through the Nightmare Realm, into an obscure corner now called "Dimension MAB-3L". Alternate Self: All different versions of Mabel. Animate Inanimate Object: The alternate Mabels include Table Mabel, Lightbulb Mabel, a flail with Mabel's face, a Mabel who's a sweater with a face on it, and a Mabel that resembles a television set. Bob Ross Rib: One of the Mabels resembles Bob Ross, donning his clothes, hair, and mustache andprioritizing painting a landscape over trying to stop Anti-Mabel from stealing Prime Mabel's ship and escaping. Cloud Cuckoo Lander: Just like Prime-Mabel, all of her alternate universe counterparts are very silly, free-spirited, and jovial. However, this would be deconstructed as these aspects of the alternate Mabels are preventing them from finding a way back to their home dimensions.

characters.name: Jersey Devil
characters.description: A cryptid Stanford and Stanley encountered in their youth in Glass Shard Beach, New Jersey. Another Dimension: Much like the bonus materials state for the Gobblewonker, it apparently fell through a rift from another dimension. Diabolus ex Nihilo: A cryptogram states it fell out of a rift straight into the Pine Barrens. The Jersey Devil: Has most of the traditional traits: horns, hooves, bat wings, and a vaguely humanoid shape. It also breathes fire. True to its name, it's one of the few monsters seen outside of Gravity Falls. Our Dragons Are Different: It has the overall appearance of a dragon, complete with fire breath, but with a goat-like head. It also has a hoard of treasure, with the Stans getting on its trail under the belief it stole their father's gold necklace.

characters.name: Silas Birchtree
characters.description: The founder of Ciphertology, a cult in the 1950s dedicated to the worship of Bill Cipher. In actuality, Silas was aSnake Oil Salesmanwho died choking on a coin he flipped and Bill possessed his corpse. Ambiguous Situation: According toThe Book of Bill, Bill can possess corpses. However, it's unclear if Bill can do this by force, or if he had to strike a deal with Silas that allowed him to take over his body even after death. Body Horror: Thanks to normal decomposition and Bill's masochism when he possesses a body, Silas' corpse rots worse and worse during "his" time running Ciphertology. When Bill left after the Kansas State Guard foiled his attempt to build a portal, "flies swarmed from [Silas'] mouth and collapsed into a grey husk." Connected All Along: On the board from thisisnotawebsite, his name is linked to Abigale Northwest (maiden name Blackwing according toThe Book of Bill), a member of the Anti-Cipher Organization. This explains why the Northwests in the show had items relating to Bill in their house. Demonic Possession: Throughout the duration of the cult's founding, the real Silas is actuallyalready dead, with Bill taking over his body.

characters.name: The Axolotl
characters.description: An otherworldly being invoked by Bill's (backward) final words, mentioned in several cryptograms in books published after the series proper concluded, and shown in an ambiguously canonicalhidden pageofDipper and Mabel and the Curse of the Time Pirates' Treasure! Always a Bigger Fish: It's implied to be much higher up the supernatural power scale than Bill is. This is best shown in how it speaks about him: it doesn't describe Bill as a fearsome dream demon, but rather a patheticSad Clowndesperately trying to shirk the consequences of his actions. True enough, Bill is completely helpless when it takes him up on his offer, but does so in a way Bill has no hope of escaping. Assuaging Axolotl: It's a benevolent, all-knowing entity...that looks like a giant pink axolotl. However, the Axolotl is very reasonable in its motives and judges based on what is best for the individual, and with Bill's fate, it's rather generous in offering him reincarnation. That is, the Axolotl stipulated its gift would only work if Bill is willing to change his ways and truly repent, since moving on from his own trauma was what Bill actually needed. Since Bill's one tosquander resurrectionfor revenge, the Axolotl has him go through indefinite rehabilitation before he can properly resurrect himself, something Bill is unlikely to ever do. Bargain with Heaven: The Axolotl's deal with Bill is that he will be resurrected/reincarnated, but only once he genuinely feels remorse and repents for his crimes. Until then, Bill is stuck in an extra-dimensional prison and is unlikely to ever change, something the Axolotl is well aware of. It's a rare example that'sexploitative toward the signatory, but still a good thing because he clearly deserves nothing better. Celestial Body: When it appears to the deceased Bill to make aBargain with Heaven, instead of appearing as a giant axolotl, it's a star-filled, ethereal being with a fire-like frill.

characters.name: The Oracle
characters.description: A mysterious, seven eyed humanoid woman who assisted Ford in his quest to defeat Bill. Exact Words: She told Ford that he has "the face of the man who's destined to destroy Bill." Extra Eyes: Her defining feature is the seven eyes on the upper half of her face. Good Counterpart: According to Ford, she and Bill have many similarities, with Ford even referring to her as a sort of anti-Bill. Mysterious Waif: She appears in only two pages ofJournal 3, assisting Ford by putting a metal plate in his head and giving him information about Bill before sending him to another dimension in his sleep.

characters.name: Scalene and Euclid
characters.description: Bill's parents, Scalene and Euclid. They were introduced inThe Book of Billvia thisisnotawebsitedotcom.com through short stories, videos, codes and even named through coffee stains on a piece of paper forming Morse code. Ambiguous Gender: It's ambiguous to which parent is named Euclid and Scalene, and that's not even getting into Bill's claims that Euclydia has over fourteen billion genders. Judging from a "traditional" naming and familial standpoint, Scalene is a hatless triangle, and is Bill's "mother", while a triangle with a top hat, more resembling Bill, is Euclid, and in turn, his "father", though it's still subject to speculation. Color-Coded for Your Convenience: Implied. On thisisnotawebsitedotcom.com, it's stated that all Bill draws are red and blue triangles. Et Tu, Brute?:Assuming the voice heard in "VALLIS CINERIS" is at least one of their voices, it's clear they feel a sense of betrayal and confusion at Bill'ssudden and accidental destruction of Euclydia and the mass manslaughter of his people."WHY DID YOU DO IT? WHY DID YOU DO IT? WHY DID YOU DO IT? WHY DID YOU DO IT?" Even Bad Men Love Their Mamas: Scalene is on the receiving end of this from the otherwise narcissistic, sociopathicBill Cipher, who immediately gets defensive (and eventually physically hostile) when Time Baby brings them up.

characters.name: The Theraprism Counselors
characters.description: The workers for a correctional facility located in the Neutral Zone of Dimension #5150 and outside of time, where deceased inter-dimensional criminals are rehabilitated to one day reincarnate. Their latest patient? None other than Bill Cipher himself. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: Their way of redeeming some of the vilest beings in the multiverse includes such things as group therapy, journaling, arts and crafts, puppet shows and cheesy motivational posters. It sounds asinine and ineffective, but as a patient listing inThe Book of Billshows, theyhavesucceeded in redeeming people. It probably helps that theywillspend all of eternity trying these methods until they work. Cool and Unusual Punishment: The ultimate prison for Bill Cipher and other inter-dimensional maniacs is group therapy sessions. For all of eternity. It's still an effective prison, though, as Bill's refusal to admit to his mistakes and desire for freedom means the place is genuinely agonizing for him. Misplaced Kindergarten Teacher: They're obnoxiously upbeat, and their recreation activities are childish, insipid things like puppet shows and arts and crafts. Keep in mind, their patients are all eons-oldEldritch Abominationvillains.

characters.name: Characters / Gravity Falls - Mystery Twins
characters.description: Acting Your Intellectual Age: A mild case, but Dipper is rather intelligent, and doesn't have many friends his own age. He prefers hanging out with 15-year-old Wendy, and the plot of "The Inconveniencing" is partially put in motion when he tries to befriend her group of friends. Achievements in Ignorance: Dipper discovers Journal 3 by complete accident within a few days of arriving in the town of Gravity Falls.Grunkle Stan was searching for that journal for30 years. Achilles' Heel: Several of them...His attraction to Wendy. It often gets him in more trouble since he tries SO hard to impress her, but often enough just winds up blowing it in some fashion or simply is unable to do anything about it at all. Doesn't help that most episodes showcasing it involve plots that force him to go against his desire to impress her in order to keep everyone safe.A couple of episodes show he's pretty ticklish, just like most other boys his age. characters.name: Characters / Gravity Falls – Bill Cipher
characters.description: Abandoned Mascot:The Book of Billreveals he used to be the mascot for a cartoon company, before critics hated him and he was abandoned and covered up. Abandonment-Induced Animosity: The Book Of Bill heavily implies he felt abandoned and rejected by his own kind, leading him to want to expand in other dimensions. Above Good and Evil: Suggested heavily byDipper and Mabel's Guide to Mystery and Nonstop Funwhere he writes "Nostradamus was a hack! Morality is a mental cage designed by the weak!How's Annie?" Above the Gods: Bill brags in the Book Of Bill about how he inspired Egyptian and Aztec gods and even ate some gods. Absurd Phobia: Typing in "Well well well being" into thisisnotawebsitedotcom three times shows Theraprism notes that Bill is afraid of3Dglasses, Venetian blinds, and TV static. Although, all three fears aren’t exactly fears as they are triggers as they remind him of his parents and home.note3D glasses are red and blue, like Scalene and Euclid, and they remind him of how alienated he felt even by them for his ability to perceive the third dimension, Venetian blinds go from horizontal to vertical, hinting at how Euclydia was destroyed when Billchanged their perspectiveand TV static sounds to Bill like the screams of his people when they all died. Early-Bird Cameo:He appears briefly in the intro of episode 1 as well as many other off-hand cameosbefore making his debut in the season 1 finale, Dreamscaperers. Eats Babies: InThe Book of Bill, he claims you can eat both a baby and a briefcase. Emotion Eater: InThe Book of Bill, he claims to literally drink fear, and it tastes like cheesecake. The End of the World as We Know It: His plan is to merge the human world with the dream world, which will destroy the world according to Ford. He dubs the event "Weirdmageddon" and as of the end of "Dipper and Mabel vs. The Future", it's begun. Energy Being: Describes himself as a being of pure energy.
